newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Overdue debt levels growing among Vietnam's banks.
newsitem.headline: Overdue debt levels growing among Vietnam's banks.

text.p: Overdue debt among commercial banks in southern Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City is growing fast with little sign of the situation easing, a state newspaper said on Friday.

The Lao Dong reported that the proportion of debt which is overdue had increased from 5.3 percent of total outstanding debt at the end of last year to around 20 percent in the first six months of this year.
It put total debts at 23,383 billion dong ($2.08 billion) as of the end of June and said 83.21 percent of this was in the form of short-term loans.

Vietnam's domestic banking system has run into serious problems this year following the collapse into scandal of several major conglomerates who had borrowed heavily to finance property speculation during a short-lived boom.

Loose management of credit by both commercial and state banks has left several facing substantial losses, currently estimated at around $675 million, and caused delays in repayments on deferred letters of credit.

Lao Dong said the situation was serious because firms who had borrowed were unlikely to be able to accelerate repayment, while collateral in the form of real estate could not be easily recovered because of Vietnam's complex land-ownership rules.

It said the authorities in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's economic hub, were examining ways of reorganising the commercial bank sector, and were expected to submit proposed changes to the government later this month for approval.
